name: Tavern Night · Thirst
summary: The Night-Owl is full of warm throats. After dark your thirst slips its leash; the sound of blood moving under every skin rises like a tide.
narrative_beats: Hearth-fire, sweat, ale. And that sound — blood moving under skin, thin, like countless streams.
The throat of the drunk at the next table rises and falls. You realize you have been staring too long.
The one in the case, almost a whisper: "Your eyes. Pull the hood down. Now."
player_options: Rise and leave, ride out to the wagon and endure it alone (safe, but thirst remains; tomorrow night is worse)
Follow a stray drunk into an alley (zeroes thirst, but almost surely leaves a corpse and rumors → suspicion spikes)
Ask Margot for a room that locks, grit it out (costs coins; pass the check and thirst eases a little, no suspicion rise)
consequences: Restraint: once more you harmed no one. Thirst doesn't zero, but you remain 'the safe one.'
Indulgence: thirst zeroes, but a body is found in town next day — suspicion spikes, the inquisitor comes, and this town is one you can likely only flee.
Caught losing control: eyes and fangs seen by another is the same as public exposure.
